overall_summary: Deduplication of 47 unique uploads reveals a stark divergence in audience retention and reach: extreme exoplanet and immersive survival what-if scenarios consistently break the 700-1,050 view threshold with strong engagement (up to 3.7% like ratio), while static psychology facts and repeated uploads plateau below 100 views. The audience strongly gravitates toward visceral, second-person immersive stakes involving extreme physics and cosmic hazards.

winning_patterns.pattern: Second-Person Extreme Environment Survival ('What If You Fell Into...')
winning_patterns.evidence: 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (1,029 views, 38 likes) and 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (972 views, 18 likes) outperformed channel baseline by over 500%.
winning_patterns.action: Frame high-concept cosmic physics as an immediate, sensory first-person survival scenario rather than passive educational trivia.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'The Planet Darker Than Coal: TrES-2b' (1,030 views, 36 likes) and 'Venus Has a Day Longer Than Its Year' (981 views, 21 likes) generated the highest organic reach.
winning_patterns.action: Center hooks around single, mind-bending scientific paradoxes that challenge baseline intuition within the first 1.5 seconds.

weak_patterns.evidence: 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' averaged under 25 views across multiple attempts (5, 10, 53 views); 'The Real Reason Songs Get Stuck In Your Head' stalled at 17 views.
weak_patterns.action: Retire generic psychology explainers that lack sensory urgency or visual spectacle.

weak_patterns.evidence: Duplicate uploads of 'Why Space Is Completely Silent' (34, 87, 220 views) and 'Octopuses Have THREE Hearts' suffered diminishing returns and low engagement.
weak_patterns.action: Enforce strict uniqueness rules; iterate on underlying concepts using entirely new astronomical entities rather than recycling topics.

next_video.concept: What happens to the human body if you approach a Magnetar (the universe's strongest magnet).
next_video.opening_direction: Start instantly with high-velocity sound design and a macro visual of blood cells: 'If you fell toward a Magnetar, you wouldn't crash into it—you'd vanish before you even arrived.'
next_video.twist_direction: Reveal that at 1,000 kilometers away, the magnetic field is so violent it tears the electron clouds of your atoms into needle-thin cylinders, dissolving your molecular structure into atomic mist in milliseconds.
next_video.reason: Leverages the proven 'extreme survival what-if' format that generated channel-high views (1,000+ views), while introducing a completely fresh cosmic object (Magnetar SGR 1806-20) instead of repeated exoplanets.
fresh_topic_constraints: Do not mention diamond planets, burning ice, glass rain, or TrES-2b
Must focus on atomic-level magnetic physics rather than standard gravity or black hole spaghettification
Ensure all physical consequences (electron distortion, diamagnetic disruption) remain strictly scientifically accurate

experiment: Test whether framing extreme cosmic phenomena around biological body horror/destruction delivers higher comments-per-view than inanimate environmental destruction.
